feature.title: Product Scope & Must-Buy
feature.contentMd:
## What It Does
Defines which products qualify for the promotion's discount (Product Scope) and which products MUST be in the order for the promo to activate (Must-Buy). These are two separate concepts:

- **Product Scope**: products whose purchase counts toward slab qualification and on which discount applies
- **Must-Buy**: mandatory products the order must contain for the promo to activate at all

## Common Questions
- **How do I specify which products a promotion applies to?** Use Product Scope — define by category, brand, sub-category, or individual SKU.
- **Can I require certain products to be in the order before the promo activates?** Yes — use Must-Buy conditions. The order must contain the specified products.
- **Can I set complex requirements like 'buy A AND B' or 'buy A OR B'?** Yes — Must-Buy supports AND, OR, and nested logic.
- **What's the difference between product scope and must-buy?** Scope determines what gets the discount. Must-buy determines what must be in the order for the promo to even activate.

## Key Difference Between Scope and Must-Buy
- Product Scope answers: 'What products does the discount apply to?'
- Must-Buy answers: 'What products must be in the order for the promo to even activate?'
- A promo can have both: must-buy to activate, then scope determines what gets the discount

## Scope
### In Scope
- Product scope definition by category, brand, SKU
- Must-buy conditions with AND/OR/nested logic
- Per-product date overrides

### Out of Scope
- Product group management (covered in Custom Product Groups)
- FOC product selection (covered in FOC Promotions)

## Who Uses It
- **Trade Marketing Manager** — configures product scope and must-buy when creating a promo
- **System** — validates must-buy conditions before applying discounts

## Rules
1. Product Scope and Must-Buy are separate lists with different purposes
2. Must-Buy supports AND/OR logic with nested grouping
3. Can be defined at any granularity: SKU, batch code, brand, category, sub-category, flavour, size, item class
4. Each must-buy item has minimum value (quantity) and unit (pieces/cases)
5. Product Bifurcations: per-product date overrides
6. A single promo commonly combines outlet + product + must-buy + FOC + budget

## Data & Fields
| Field | Description | Required | Example |
|-------|-------------|----------|--------|
| Product Scope | Products qualifying for discount | Yes | Category = Beverages |
| Must-Buy Product | Mandatory product | No | SKU-PEPSI-500ML |
| Must-Buy Quantity | Minimum qty required | No | 10 |
| Must-Buy Unit | UOM | No | Case / Piece |
| Comparator | AND/OR logic | No | AND |
| Parent Comparator | Nested group logic | No | OR |

## Tenant-Level Configurations
| Config Point | Options | Default | Example |
|-------------|---------|---------|--------|
| Product attribute targeting | Maps product attributes to targeting criteria | Tenant-specific | Brand, Category |
| Must-buy validation | Strict / Lenient | Strict | How strictly must-buy is enforced |

scenarios.title: Product Scope — What Counts Toward Slab Qualification
scenarios.contentMd:
## What It Does
The product scope determines which products in an order are counted toward slab qualification and which receive the discount. Products outside the scope are completely ignored.

## Example
1. A promo has Product Scope = Beverages category
2. The promo has: Slab 1 (50+ cases → 10% off)
3. An order contains: 60 cases of beverages + 30 cases of snacks
4. System identifies that only beverages are in scope
5. Only the 60 cases of beverages count toward slab qualification
6. 60 ≥ 50 → qualifies for Slab 1 → 10% discount applied to beverages only
7. The 30 cases of snacks are completely ignored — no discount, no counting

## Example — Scope by Brand
A promo targets Brand = Pepsi specifically:
- Order has 20 cases of Pepsi, 15 cases of 7Up, 10 cases of Mirinda
- Product scope = Pepsi brand only
- Only the 20 cases of Pepsi count toward qualification
- 7Up and Mirinda are ignored even though they are from the same company

## Example — Scope by Individual SKU
A promo targets SKU = SKU-PEPSI-500ML:
- Order has 50 × Pepsi 500ml + 30 × Pepsi 1L
- Only 50 × Pepsi 500ml is counted — 1L is out of scope

## Rules
1. Product Scope defines WHICH products are eligible for the promo's benefit
2. Products outside scope are ignored during slab calculation
3. Scope can be defined by category, brand, sub-category, individual SKU, or any combination
4. Product targeting works the same way as outlet targeting — using configurable criteria mapped to product attributes

scenarios.title: Must-Buy Conditions with AND/OR Logic
scenarios.contentMd:
## What It Does
Must-buy conditions are mandatory requirements that an order must meet before a promo can activate. Unlike product scope, must-buy doesn't define what gets the discount — it defines the prerequisite for the promo to even apply.

## Example — Simple Must-Buy (AND logic)
A promo requires: Must buy 10+ cases of Pepsi 500ml AND 5+ cases of 7Up 500ml.
- Order has 15 cases Pepsi 500ml + 8 cases 7Up 500ml → ✓ Both conditions met → promo activates
- Order has 15 cases Pepsi 500ml + 3 cases 7Up 500ml → ✗ 7Up is below minimum → promo does NOT activate
- Order has 15 cases Pepsi 500ml only (no 7Up) → ✗ Missing 7Up → promo does NOT activate

## Example — OR Logic
A promo requires: Must buy 10+ cases of Pepsi 500ml OR 10+ cases of 7Up 500ml.
- Order has 12 cases Pepsi 500ml (no 7Up) → ✓ Pepsi condition met → promo activates
- Order has 0 Pepsi + 15 cases 7Up → ✓ 7Up condition met → promo activates
- Order has 5 Pepsi + 5 7Up → ✗ Neither condition met → promo does NOT activate

## Example — Nested Logic (AND groups combined with OR)
A promo requires: (Pepsi 500ml × 10 AND Lays × 5) OR (7Up 500ml × 10 AND Kurkure × 5)
- This creates two groups:
  - Group 1: Pepsi + Lays
  - Group 2: 7Up + Kurkure
- The order must meet ALL conditions in at least ONE group
- Order with 10 Pepsi + 5 Lays → ✓ Group 1 met → promo activates
- Order with 10 7Up + 5 Kurkure → ✓ Group 2 met → promo activates
- Order with 10 Pepsi + 5 Kurkure → ✗ Neither group fully met → promo does NOT activate

## Rules
1. Must-buy is checked BEFORE slab qualification — if must-buy fails, the promo doesn't apply at all
2. AND logic: ALL conditions in the group must be met
3. OR logic: any ONE condition in the group being met is sufficient
4. Nested logic: AND groups combined with OR allow complex requirements
5. Each must-buy item specifies: product (SKU/brand/category), minimum quantity, and unit (pieces/cases)
